findings.observation: Reviewed the sheet index on Sheet 1 (Cover Sheet) using the vision tool. The index lists 52 sheets covering civil, grading, utilities, landscaping, building plans, and survey sheets. No sheet is titled 'Addressing Plan' or any variation containing 'address' or 'addressing'. The addressing information appears to be integrated into the site plan sheets (Sheets 13-15) rather than on a dedicated addressing plan sheet.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires addressing information to be shown on either a dedicated 'Addressing Plan sheet' OR 'the overall site plan sheet', and to be listed in the sheet index. While the addressing information may be present on the site plan sheets themselves, there is no dedicated addressing plan sheet listed in the sheet index. The item states this as a deficiency when addressing is 'not shown on an Addressing Plan sheet or the overall site plan sheet, or not listed in Sheet Index'. Since no dedicated sheet exists and is not listed, this is technically a deficiency even though the information may be present on other sheets.
findings.explanation: No 'Addressing Plan' sheet is listed in the sheet index on Sheet 1. Addressing information appears integrated into site plan sheets rather than on a dedicated sheet.
findings.resolution: Add a dedicated 'Addressing Plan' sheet to the plan set and list it in the sheet index, or clearly label one of the existing site plan sheets (e.g., Sheet 13, 14, or 15) as the 'Addressing Plan' sheet in the sheet index.

findings.observation: Used vision tool to examine Sheet 14 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan 1 of 2). The sheet includes a Key Notes section (Block 3) that defines numbered callouts used throughout the plan. Key Note 7 is labeled 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE'. The legend (Block 5) includes a triangle symbol defined as 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE'. Visual inspection of the site plan drawing confirms these triangle symbols with '7' callouts are placed at multiple locations around the building perimeter, identifying entrance points.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires main front entrance, building doors, entries, and access points to be labeled on the site plan. The evidence shows building entrances are clearly identified through both symbolic notation (triangles) and numbered callouts (Key Note 7) on Sheet 14, with the legend providing explicit definition. This meets the requirement for labeling building entries and access points on the plan.
findings.explanation: Building entrances are labeled on Sheet 14 using Key Note 7 callouts with triangle symbols defined in the legend as 'PROPOSED BUILDING ENTRANCE'.

findings.observation: Examined Sheets 14, 15 (site plans) and Sheet 37 (Building Plan - Level 1 parking garage) using vision tool. Sheet 14 blocks.md shows Key Notes including 'PROPOSED FIRE HYDRANT' (note 4) and 'PROPOSED ADA RAMP' (note 12), and the legend includes 'PROPOSED ADA PATH'. Driveway access points are visible on the site plan drawings along Collier Street. Sheet 37 vision check confirmed handicap parking spaces are labeled with 'HC', 'VAN', and wheelchair symbols throughout the garage level. The parking garage building is clearly shown on site plan sheets. Sidewalk access is indicated by ADA path symbols and ramp callouts.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is that driveway access points, handicap parking, garages, and sidewalk access be 'identified' on plans. (1) Driveway access points: visible and dimensioned on site plan sheets along Collier Street frontage; (2) Handicap parking: clearly labeled on parking garage plan (Sheet 37) with standard accessibility notation; (3) Garage: the parking garage building is shown and labeled on site plan sheets; (4) Sidewalk access: ADA paths are shown in the legend and ADA ramps are called out via Key Note 12. All four required elements are identified on the plans.
findings.explanation: Driveway access points shown on site plans (Sheets 14-15); handicap parking labeled on garage plan (Sheet 37) with HC/VAN symbols; garage building identified on site plans; sidewalk access shown via ADA path symbols and ramp callouts.

findings.observation: Used vision tool to examine the Cover Sheet (Sheet 1). The project name displayed prominently at the top center of the sheet is '1700 SOUTH LAMAR'. This title appears in the main project identification area as well as in the title block. The project name begins with the address number '1700' followed by the street name 'SOUTH LAMAR'.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item flags project names that include an address number (e.g., '1515 Main St Commons') rather than a descriptive project name (e.g., 'Main St Commons'). The project name '1700 SOUTH LAMAR' is literally the street address rather than a descriptive project name. Per CC Submittal Checklist p.2 and 911 Addressing Standards, project names should not begin with a street address number. This is marked as 'warn' status in the checklist table, indicating it should be corrected but may be a lower-priority deficiency.
findings.explanation: Project name '1700 SOUTH LAMAR' begins with the address number '1700', contrary to 911 Addressing Standards requiring descriptive project names without address numbers.
findings.resolution: Revise the project name to a descriptive name that does not begin with the street address number. For example, use 'South Lamar Commons' or similar descriptive name instead of '1700 SOUTH LAMAR'.

findings.observation: Reviewed Sheet 13 (Overall Site & Paving & Striping Plan), Sheet 14-15 (Dimensional Control & Site Plan), and Sheet 16 (Site Notes and Tables) pre-processed data. Sheet 13 guide.md identifies 'Proposed Building 1 Area: 133,718 SF'. Sheet 16 blocks.md shows the Building Information table lists only 'STRUCTURE 1' for the site plan. No references to Building 2, Building 3, or multiple building structures were found in any of the reviewed sheets or data tables.
findings.reasoning: This checklist item applies conditionally: 'If multiple buildings' are present, they must be labeled sequentially (Bldg 1, Bldg 2, etc.) per 911 Addressing Standards p.8. The site plan shows only a single building structure (Proposed Building 1 / Structure 1) for this mixed-use development. Since there is only one building, the condition 'If multiple buildings' is not met, making this item not applicable to the current site plan.
findings.explanation: Only one building (Proposed Building 1) is shown on the site plan. Sequential building labeling requirement applies only when multiple buildings are present.

findings.observation: Read Sheet 16 blocks.md, which contains the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - PROJECT TRACKING TABLE'. The table includes columns for 'TOTAL FLOOR AREA RATIO' with three sub-columns: 'MAX ALLOWED', 'TOTAL FLOOR AREA (GSF) PROPOSED', 'PROPOSED FAR', and 'ALLOWED FAR'. The bottom row shows 'PROPOSED FAR' as '2.14:1' and 'ALLOWED FAR' as '4:1'. Both proposed and allowed FAR values are clearly displayed in the data table.
findings.reasoning: The checklist requires the data table to show both proposed FAR and allowed FAR values. The Project Tracking Table on Sheet 16 explicitly presents both metrics side-by-side: the proposed FAR (2.14:1) and the maximum allowed FAR (4:1). This provides the necessary comparison for zoning compliance review. The requirement is fully satisfied.
findings.explanation: Data table on Sheet 16 shows both proposed FAR (2.14:1) and allowed FAR (4:1) in the Project Tracking Table.

findings.observation: Read Sheet 16 blocks.md containing the 'PROJECT BUILDING UNITS TABLE'. This table shows a breakdown by unit type: 70 Studio units, 328 1-Bedroom units, 55 2-Bedroom units, and 6 3-Bedroom units. The table does not show an explicit total, but summing these values yields 459 total units. Additionally, the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - PARKING TABLE' on the same sheet lists the proposed use-mix including Studio (70 units), 1 Bedroom (328 units), 2 Bedroom (55 units), and 3 Bedroom (6 units), confirming the unit count.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is for the data table to include the unit count. The Project Building Units Table provides a detailed breakdown of all 459 residential units by type (Studio, 1-BR, 2-BR, 3-BR). While there is no single cell labeled 'Total Units', the unit count is clearly presented in tabular form and can be readily verified by addition. This satisfies the intent of the requirement, which is to provide unit count information in the data table for review.
findings.explanation: Data table on Sheet 16 includes unit count: 70 Studio, 328 1-Bedroom, 55 2-Bedroom, 6 3-Bedroom units (total 459 units) in the Project Building Units Table.

findings.observation: Read Sheet 16 blocks.md containing the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - BUILDING INFORMATION' table. This table includes columns for 'STORIES' and 'HEIGHT'. The values shown are '6' for stories and '81.02' for height in feet. Both the number of stories and the height in feet are clearly stated in the data table.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is for the data table to include both building height in feet and in stories. The Building Information table provides both metrics: 6 stories and 81.02 feet. This information is necessary for verifying compliance with zoning height limits and compatibility standards. The requirement is satisfied.
findings.explanation: Data table on Sheet 16 includes building height in both stories (6) and feet (81.02) in the Building Information table.

findings.observation: Read Sheet 16 blocks.md containing the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - BUILDING INFORMATION' table. This table includes a 'TOTAL SF' column with a floor-by-floor breakdown: Floor 1 (64,065 SF), Floor 2 (76,137 SF), Floor 3 (77,476 SF), Floor 4 (77,476 SF), Floor 5 (77,476 SF), Floor 6 (52,793 SF), with a 'TOTAL GSF' row showing 425,424 SF. The table identifies this as 'STRUCTURE 1'. The gross floor area is provided both per building level and as an overall total.
findings.reasoning: The requirement is for the data table to include gross floor area 'per building and/or overall total'. Since there is only one building structure on this site plan, the table provides the floor-by-floor breakdown (effectively the per-building GFA broken down by level) and the overall total GFA of 425,424 SF. This information is critical for FAR calculations and for determining whether the 250,000 SF OWRS threshold is triggered. The requirement is satisfied.
findings.explanation: Data table on Sheet 16 includes GFA per floor (64,065 to 77,476 SF per level) and overall total (425,424 GSF) in the Building Information table.

findings.observation: Read Sheet 16 blocks.md containing the '1700 SOUTH LAMAR - PROJECT TRACKING TABLE'. The table includes a column labeled 'PROPOSED OPEN SPACE (5% required)' with three sub-columns for (AC), (SF), and (%). The bottom TOTAL row shows values of 0.26 AC, 11,350 SF, and 5%. findings.reasoning: This checklist item applies conditionally: 'If open space requirement applies to zoning district'. The Project Tracking Table column header states '(5% required)', confirming that open space IS required for this site's zoning. The table then provides both the percentage (5%) and square footage (11,350 SF) for the proposed open space. Since the requirement applies and the data is present, the item passes.
findings.explanation: Data table on Sheet 16 includes open space percentage (5%) and square footage (11,350 SF). The column header confirms open space is required for this zoning district.

findings.observation: Read the Consolidated Site Plan Application supplementary document, Section 6 (Property Attributes). Line 28 asks: 'Is your project on a Hill Country Roadway?' with checkboxes for Yes and No. The 'No' box is checked (marked with [x]). Additionally, reviewed facts.md which shows the site is located at 1700 S Lamar Blvd, and the Principal Street Type is listed as 'Core Transit Corridor' on line 30 of the application (not 'Hill Country Roadway'). Semantic search for Hill Country Roadway or LDC 25-2-1101 references returned no relevant results from the plan set.
findings.reasoning: This checklist item applies conditionally: 'If within Hill Country Roadway Corridor per LDC 25-2-1101--1107'. The Hill Country Roadway Corridor applies to sites within 1,000 feet of Loop 360, RM 620, RM 2222, RM 2244, or Southwest Parkway. The Consolidated Site Plan Application explicitly indicates the project is NOT on a Hill Country Roadway. The site address (1700 S Lamar Blvd) is not near any of the five designated Hill Country Roadways. Since the triggering condition is not met, this item is not applicable.
findings.explanation: Consolidated Site Plan Application (Section 6, line 28) confirms the project is NOT on a Hill Country Roadway. HCR requirements do not apply.
